A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Schur-complement research, despite the changed title and organization. Their text, equations, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original diversity evaluations, CLIP decomposition experiments, captioning analyses and typographic-attack results, including supplementary experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds CLEVR, country-text and alternative-embedding evaluations.

M1.justification: The stated score changes from weighted entropy in v2 Equation 8 to its exponential in v3 Definition 1. This changes the defined output beyond renaming SCE to Scendi, while retaining the underlying Schur-complement and residual-embedding framework.

E1.justification: V3 adds controlled CLEVR shape scenarios and a text-to-text task using country prompts and DeepSeek-generated factual responses. These substantially extend coverage beyond the retained image-generation, captioning and typographic-attack tasks.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Vendi, RKE, Recall/Coverage and the unchanged or naive-subtraction CLIP controls where applicable. Conditional Vendi is discussed but not evaluated. The additional embedding variants test Scendi itself rather than introduce competing diversity methods.

E3.justification: V3 adds CLEVR prompts with and without shape information, country-count sweeps from 10 to 50, and alternative embedding configurations. The stated metric now exponentiates entropy. Existing settings such as 2,000 Fourier features, 1,000 images per breed and 5,000 MSCOCO captions remain; these revisions do not establish rerunning retained experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix F and Figure 22 add embedding-sensitivity tests on the existing cat-breed dataset using OpenCLIP, a FairCLIP/Fare-CLIP-labeled variant and BLIP2. CLEVR adds a controlled prompt-specificity check. Existing kernel comparisons, typographic analyses and naive-subtraction ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the mention of different seeds for the four doctor-image sets. Neither introduces repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or another uncertainty-estimation procedure; the added results continue point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial results for the new tasks and embeddings. Figure 7 reports CLEVR Scendi scores of 2.94, 2.95 and 2.96 with shape information versus 2.53, 2.96 and 3.70 without it; Figures 8 and 22 add country-text and embedding trends. These extend the evidence under new settings, while corresponding legacy numerical results are largely retained.

T1.justification: V3 mathematically redefines the score through exponentiation and changes the main-text conversion matrix from C_TI C_TT^{-1} to C_IT C_TT^{-1}. Appendix A largely retains the earlier derivations and shared-eigenvector assumption, including formulas not synchronized with these main-text revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract now explicitly claims successful diversity evaluation of text-to-text LLMs and broadens the framing to prompt-guided generative models. The central contributions of separating prompt-driven and model-driven diversity and removing CLIP concept directions remain.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly explains applicability to unimodal tasks without cross-modal embeddings, and Appendix F qualifies robustness as dependent on the embedding. Appendix B nevertheless states a cross-modal-only restriction, leaving tension in the revised applicability discussion.

D1.justification: V3 adds embedding/backbone identifiers for the new experiments, including Qwen3-0.6B and Figure 22's configurations, and updates the advertised repository location from CLIP-DISSECTION to scendi-score. The middle robustness model is inconsistently labeled FairCLIP and Fare-CLIP, limiting identification of that configuration.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning through concurrent Conditional Vendi, Truncated Vendi, CLIP geometry and semantic guidance, plus kernel-based model selection, novelty and embedding-alignment research. This adds substantive relationships to prior work beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: V3 retitles the paper and metric, rewrites the abstract and introductory framing, and reorganizes the narrative around prompt-aware diversity. Much captioning and diffusion discussion moves out of the main text, while the appendices gain separate limitations, captioning and robustness sections.

P2.justification: The main text switches to two columns, introductory figures are reordered and trimmed, and many existing figures move to appendices. KPCA and t-SNE panels are rearranged or reduced, while new CLEVR, country-text and embedding-robustness displays substantially revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The CLEVR controls strengthen evidence that the score separates prompt information from image diversity, and the alternative-embedding tests substantiate compatibility previously asserted more broadly. These provide a limited overall improvement. The gains are constrained by inconsistent main-text and appendix score formulas and the conflict between Section 5's unimodal applicability and Appendix B's cross-modal-only limitation.
